beats.narration_en: Why does this guardrail end peel into a steel ribbon?
Because a plain rail end does this. It spears right into the cabin.
So the end gets a steel head that slides down the rail.
Inside, it squeezes the rail flat and bends it away.
Crushing steel takes a huge force, and that force slows the car.
The posts snap off, so nothing snags the wheels.
Sixty to zero in about two car lengths, and the cabin is untouched.
So next time you pass a yellow guardrail head, you know what it is waiting for.
